question: Can heap limits and DFA cache policy be recorded, preflighted, and enforced in control/candidate comparison without changing parser behavior or requiring a larger heap for small campaigns?
control: Pre-change production reports recorded raw DFA cache environment text but not the effective heap limit, so an unsafe full-corpus campaign started and failed near the end, and comparison did not reject different execution identities.
change: Probe the TypeScript harness runtime for its effective V8 heap limit and record it with the DFA cache policy in every production report.
Reject a persistent-cache production-scale campaign below 8,192 MiB before the first file, unless --allow-unsafe-heap is explicit.
Reject comparison of campaigns with different heap or cache identities unless --allow-policy-mismatch is explicit, and record the override.
Distinguish the benchmark heap from production guidance in the report and contract.
acceptance: Every TypeScript campaign report states the effective heap limit and cache policy.
Full-corpus runs fail early with an actionable message when configuration is known unsafe.
Comparisons cannot silently mix persistent-cache, bounded-cache, or different-heap campaigns.
Quick and public workflows remain usable without requiring an 8 GB heap.
No automatic heap increase is hidden from the operator.
